title: Controls walkthrough scratchpad (prep for security review)
content:
Context:
Quick personal notes for the 1:1 controls walkthrough with Alex (audit liaison). Aim: run through our SOC2 scoping decisions, show evidence collection progress, and surface vendor controls and remaining gaps for ISO annex updates. Meeting scheduled 2026-03-06 10:00am PT (30m).

Top goals for the call:
- Confirm scope boundaries: hosted API + Dedicated (customer-managed config) included; Private on-prem excluded unless customer requested in last 6 months.
- Validate which controls we plan to test using operational logs vs process narratives (prefer logs where possible).
- Reconcile vendor list (top-10 by spend + security-critical) and confirm which require bridge letters / SOC reports.
- Agree on a short evidence delivery timeline and one escalation contact if evidence items missing.

Quick status snapshot (what I'll say):
- Evidence collection: ~72% complete for SOC2 CC1-CC7. Most missing items are around change management (CC6) and logical access review logs (CC5).
- ISO27001 Annex A mapping: initial draft done; need to update 12.5 (handling of removable media) and 8.1 (asset inventory accuracy).
- Vendor risk: three vendors flagged high (Identity provider: AuthzCo, Monitoring: LogStream, Managed infra: BeamStack). AuthzCo has SOC2 Type II (Q4 2025), LogStream has SOC2 Type II in review, BeamStack has only security questionnaire so far.

Notes / talking points to raise:
- Change management evidence: we have JIRA workflow screenshots + release calendar, but auditors prefer commit -> deploy trace for 2 sample releases. Action: ask SRE for one-week deploy trace (ticket ENG-3417).
- Logical access: Okta activity logs exist but retention for admin events only 90 days. Auditor may request 12-month trace for sampled period. Ask IAM owner about extended export (Lina).
- Automated user provisioning mapping (SCIM) — confirm record of deprovisioned users for last 12 months.
- Encryption at rest: confirm keys are KMS-managed and rotation policy exists (security ops to confirm rotation log).
- Backup verification: we run daily backups; need last 3 restore-test results.

Vendor risk specifics to discuss:
- BeamStack (managed infra): ask auditor whether current evidence (security questionnaire + recent pen-test summary) suffices or if a penetration attestation is requested. Plan: pursue a short attestation if requested (owner: Ethan).
- LogStream (monitoring): their SOC report is delayed — propose compensating control: dual-streaming critical logs to internal S3 + LogStream until report arrives. Need architecture diagram and retention policy.
- AuthzCo (IdP): show contract excerpt with SLA + their SOC2. Highlight SCIM provisioning and role mapping docs.

Open questions I want Alex to clarify:
- For controls that map to GCP-managed services (Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL), will auditor accept GCP shared-responsibility evidence or do they require our integration-level tests?
- Vendor sampling: is top-10 by spend the right approach, or do they prefer top-10 by data-sensitivity exposure?
- For ISO mapping, is evidence tied to the same artifacts we’re collecting for SOC2 acceptable, or do they expect separate Annex-level artifacts?

Evidence checklist (what to surface in the call) — mark status inline:
- Access reviews: most recent quarterly access review (DONE) — provide exported CSV (SEC-402).
- MFA enforcement policy + enforcement logs (PENDING) — need logs for 6 admin users.
- Change management: release notes + deploy traces (PENDING) — ask ENG (ENG-3417).
- Backup restore tests (PENDING) — ops to provide last 3 restores (ticket OPS-77).
- Incident response playbook + one post-mortem for last 12 months (DONE).
- Vendor contracts (PARTIAL) — most contracts attached in vendor vault, but need signed BAAs for two partners.

Immediate action items (after the call) — draft owners and rough due-dates:
- Lina: attempt Okta admin event export for Jan–Dec 2025 (due 2026-03-10).
- Ethan: request BeamStack attestation flow + push for LogStream SOC timeline (due 2026-03-12).
- SRE (assigned: Marcus): provide commit->deploy trace for two sample releases in Jan & Feb 2026 (ENG-3417, due 2026-03-11).
- Ops: attach last 3 restore test reports to evidence folder (OPS-77, due 2026-03-09).
- Me (Priya): update control mapping doc in Confluence, add notes from this call and mark gaps (due 2026-03-08).

Risk notes / pain points to flag:
- Retention mismatches: several providers keep only 90 days of admin logs; auditor often requests 12 months which triggers export work and potential storage cost. Need to estimate cost of extended retention for decision.
- BeamStack contract: no explicit SOC clause; could complicate attestation scope if they host customer data blobs.
- Evidence fragmentation: some artifacts live in GitHub, some in Confluence, some in vendor vault — propose single index doc (Confluence -> evidence checklist) to reduce back-and-forth.

Prep script (short demo actions I can show in 5m):
1) Open control mapping Confluence page (show mapping table for CC4-CC6).
2) Open evidence folder (show completed items and 3 pending items).
3) Quick peek at Okta logs export (show retention window).
4) Vendor table: show BeamStack and LogStream rows + current status.

Slack prompts I'll send before the meeting (quick DM templates):
- To Marcus (SRE): "Hey — Alex from audit will want deploy traces for Jan/Feb samples. Can you pull commit->deploy trace for two releases and attach to ENG-3417? Need by Thu. Thx!"
- To Lina (IAM): "Can you try a full Okta admin events export for 2025 and confirm if we can get 12 months raw? If not, what steps to enable it?"

Follow-up cadence recommendation (for after auditor check-in):
- Weekly evidence triage sync (30m) with SRE/IAM/Ops until all pending items closed.
- Ad-hoc vendor escalation meeting only if auditor requests deeper vendor evidence.

Notes-to-self / things to record after the call:
- Which controls auditor prioritizes for testing (they usually pick 3 focus controls).
- Any concession on retention windows (if they accept sampling instead of full 12 months).
- Exact list of vendor evidence they will accept (SOC report vs attestation vs questionnaire).

Misc references to paste into Confluence after meeting:
- Confluence control mapping: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SOC2/Control-Mapping-2026
- Evidence folder (shared drive): drive://shared_drives/company/security/evidence-2026
- Slack thread: #sec-audit-2026

End of scratchpad. Keep minimal notes in the meeting and convert to a cleaner action list in Confluence afterwards.
